273	///
274	/// **The rule**, in order: secure input held by any process (read at delivery) → nothing, not
275	/// even a time; an auto-repeat → a typed mark; ⌘ or ⌃ held, or ⌥ held with an arrow, Delete,
276	/// Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc (`optionKeyCodes`, the owner's answer of
277	/// 2026-11-01) → a shortcut; anything else → a typed mark. ⇧ alone never makes a shortcut, and
278	/// ⌥ with any other key types a character (⌥E is é), so it is typed.
279	///
280	/// **The spelling**: the held modifiers in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`, then the
281	/// key — `namedKeys` by its virtual key code, else the character lowercased, `+` spelled `plus`,
282	/// and an empty, whitespace or control character `key<code>` — joined by `+`, so the core's
283	/// check (`cursor_file_check.rs`) accepts every one this writes.
284	enum CursorKeyFilter {
285	    /// ← → ↓ ↑ (123 124 125 126), Delete (51), Forward Delete (117), Return (36), keypad Enter
286	    /// (76), Tab (48) and Esc (53): the keys ⌥ alone makes a shortcut of. Their spellings are
287	    /// the core's `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`.
288	    static let optionKeyCodes: Set<Int> = [123, 124, 125, 126, 51, 117, 36, 76, 48, 53]
289	
290	    /// The keys spelled by name, by their kVK codes (Carbon's `Events.h`).
291	    static let namedKeys: [Int: String] = [
292	        36: "return", 76: "enter", 48: "tab", 49: "space", 51: "delete", 117: "forwarddelete",
293	        53: "esc", 123: "left", 124: "right", 125: "down", 126: "up", 115: "home", 119: "end",
294	        116: "pageup", 121: "pagedown", 114: "help",
295	        122: "f1", 120: "f2", 99: "f3", 118: "f4", 96: "f5", 97: "f6", 98: "f7", 100: "f8",
296	        101: "f9", 109: "f10", 103: "f11", 111: "f12", 105: "f13", 107: "f14", 113: "f15",
297	        106: "f16", 64: "f17", 79: "f18", 80: "f19", 90: "f20",
298	    ]
299	
300	    /// Whether the key-down is a shortcut: not an auto-repeat, and ⌘ or ⌃ held, or ⌥ held with
301	    /// one of `optionKeyCodes`. The source reads a character only when this is true.
302	    static func isShortcut(_ event: CursorKeyEvent) -> Bool {
303	        guard !event.isRepeat else { return false }
304	        if event.modifiers.contains(.cmd) || event.modifiers.contains(.ctrl) { return true }
305	        return event.modifiers.contains(.opt) && optionKeyCodes.contains(event.keyCode)
306	    }
307	
308	    /// The shortcut's `+`-joined spelling (the type doc).
309	    static func spelled(_ event: CursorKeyEvent) -> String {
310	        var tokens: [String] = []
311	        if event.modifiers.contains(.cmd) { tokens.append("cmd") }
312	        if event.modifiers.contains(.ctrl) { tokens.append("ctrl") }
313	        if event.modifiers.contains(.opt) { tokens.append("opt") }
314	        if event.modifiers.contains(.shift) { tokens.append("shift") }
315	        tokens.append(keyName(event))
316	        return tokens.joined(separator: "+")
317	    }

319	    /// The key's own token: its name, else its character, else `key<code>`.
320	    private static func keyName(_ event: CursorKeyEvent) -> String {
321	        if let name = namedKeys[event.keyCode] { return name }
322	        let character = (event.character ?? "").lowercased()
323	        let plain =
324	            !character.isEmpty
325	            && character.unicodeScalars.allSatisfy { scalar in
326	                !scalar.properties.isWhitespace
327	                    && scalar.properties.generalCategory != .control
328	                    && scalar.properties.generalCategory != .format
329	            }
330	        guard plain else { return "key\(event.keyCode)" }
331	        return character.replacingOccurrences(of: "+", with: "plus")
332	    }
333	
334	    /// The whole rule (the type doc): `secure` is `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` at delivery.
335	    static func entry(for event: CursorKeyEvent, secure: Bool) -> CursorKeyEntry {
336	        if secure { return .none }
337	        if event.isRepeat { return .typed }
338	        guard isShortcut(event) else { return .typed }
339	        return .shortcut(keys: spelled(event), code: event.keyCode)
340	    }

345	/// Every screen recording's cursor file (road map creator-jobs CU1b1, spec §11 CU-11…CU-13,
346	/// CU-18): the segments' header and opening geometry, the capture's start with segment 0 open,
347	/// and the walker's cursor step, which writes one `<stem>.fjcursor` beside each landed movie
348	/// (`CursorFileWriter`, CU-15). `CursorCapture.swift` is the capture itself.
349	///
350	/// **The anchor is E1** (CU-12): a segment's times count from its screen did-start's host time,
351	/// stamped on every segment by `+Delegates.swift`; E2 is never used for a cursor file. A landed
352	/// segment with no E1 gets no file. **The geometry** comes from the frame watch (CU-13); a watch
353	/// that could not go on the stream (at the start, with no camera, or at the segment's resume)
354	/// leaves the file only its opening geometry, and the segment says so. **A cursor failure never
355	/// fails or reorders a segment** (CU-14): the walker's order is movie → microphone → camera →
356	/// cursor, and this step always hands its segment on. **Keys** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec
357	/// §11 CU-60, CU-61): with Record shortcuts on, the capture's key tap writes each shortcut and
358	/// a time-only typed mark into the open segment; `recordsKeys` is what the status item's
359	/// keyboard mark reads.
360	extension ScreenRecorder {
361	    /// MAIN. Whether the running session's cursor capture has a key tap (spec §11 CU-61).
362	    var recordsKeys: Bool { session?.cursor?.recordsKeys ?? false }
363	
364	    /// The header and opening geometry every segment's file starts from (CU-13), before any
365	    /// frame: `scale_factor` the filter's `pointPixelScale`; `content_scale` the stream's
366	    /// configured pixel width ÷ (scale factor × point width); `content_rect` (0, 0, the point
367	    /// size × content scale); `screen_rect` the source's frame — `CGDisplayBounds` for a
368	    /// display, the window list's `kCGWindowBounds` for a window (the filter's `contentRect`
369	    /// when the list has none, whose origin may be window-local rather than global points
370	    /// until the first frame's geometry replaces it), the filter's `contentRect` for a picked
371	    /// source. The header's
372	    /// `pixels_per_point` is the configured width ÷ the point width; `in_picture` the choice's
373	    /// (spec §11 CU-31: true only In the picture, where the stream burns the pointer in);
374	    /// `cursor_image` none (CU-S1).
375	    static func cursorStart(
376	        filter: SCContentFilter, choice: RecordingChoice, stream: SCStreamConfiguration
377	    ) -> CursorSegmentStart {
378	        let points = filter.contentRect.size
379	        let width = Double(max(stream.width, 1))
380	        let height = Double(max(stream.height, 1))
381	        let scaleFactor = positive(Double(filter.pointPixelScale))
382	        let pixelsPerPoint = positive(points.width > 0 ? width / Double(points.width) : 1)
383	        let contentScale = positive(
384	            points.width > 0 ? width / (scaleFactor * Double(points.width)) : 1)
385	        let source: CursorSourceKind
386	        let displayID: UInt32?
387	        let frame: CGRect
388	        switch choice.source {
389	        case .display(let id):
390	            source = .display
391	            displayID = id
392	            frame = CGDisplayBounds(id)
393	        case .window(let id):
394	            source = .window
395	            displayID = nil
396	            frame = windowBounds(id) ?? filter.contentRect
397	        case .picked, .voiceOver, .camera:
398	            source = .picked
399	            displayID = nil
400	            frame = filter.contentRect
401	        }
402	        let geometry = CursorGeometry(
403	            screenRect: frame,
404	            contentRect: CGRect(
405	                x: 0, y: 0, width: Double(points.width) * contentScale,
406	                height: Double(points.height) * contentScale),
407	            contentScale: contentScale, scaleFactor: scaleFactor)
408	        return CursorSegmentStart(
409	            inPicture: choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture, source: source,
410	            displayID: displayID, sourceFrame: frame,
411	            pointSize: points, pixelsPerPoint: pixelsPerPoint,
412	            contentSize: CursorPixelSize(
413	                width: min(Int(width), 16384), height: min(Int(height), 16384)),
414	            cursorImage: .none, geometry: geometry)
415	    }
416	
417	    /// What a Separate segment's no-file sentences end with (spec §11 CU-31 (d)): the stream drew
418	    /// no pointer, so without the file the pointer is nowhere.
419	    static let cursorSeparateLost =
420	        " The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
421	
422	    /// A segment's `cursorProblem` once its file was attempted: the writer's sentence when it
423	    /// has one (no file was kept), with `cursorSeparateLost` when `separate`; else, when the
424	    /// frames could not be watched, CU-13's sentence naming the movie and the reason (a file
425	    /// exists, so it is the same for both choices); else nil.
426	    static func cursorProblem(
427	        writer: String?, watchLost: String?, movieName: String, separate: Bool = false
428	    ) -> String? {
429	        if let writer { return separate ? writer + cursorSeparateLost : writer }
430	        guard let watchLost else { return nil }
431	        return "The cursor file for \(movieName) has only the geometry the screen had when it "
432	            + "began: its frames could not be watched (\(watchLost)), so a move or resize of "
433	            + "what was recorded after that is not in it."
434	    }
435	
436	    /// CU-12's sentence for a landed segment with no E1, with `cursorSeparateLost` when
437	    /// `separate` (CU-31 (d)).
438	    static func cursorNoAnchorProblem(movieName: String, separate: Bool = false) -> String {
439	        "The cursor file for \(movieName) was not written: the screen never reported its start, "
440	            + "so its times have nothing to count from." + (separate ? cursorSeparateLost : "")
441	    }
442	
443	    /// MAIN, from `launchScreen`: segment 0 opened, then the poll and the monitors started.
444	    /// Nothing for a session without a capture.
445	    func startCursorCapture() {
446	        guard let current = session, let cursor = current.cursor, let start = current.cursorStart
447	        else { return }
448	        cursor.openSegment(0, start)
449	        cursor.start()
450	    }
451	
452	    /// The walker's cursor step for segment `index`, after its camera's: the buffer closed
453	    /// with the movie's track size and E1, written beside the movie on the capture's queue,
454	    /// and `landed` handed to `then` on main with its cursor fields. A session without a
455	    /// capture hands `landed` on unchanged.
456	    func saveCursor(
457	        _ done: Session, at index: Int, _ landed: RecordingSegment,
458	        then: @escaping (RecordingSegment) -> Void
459	    ) {
460	        guard let cursor = done.cursor else { return then(landed) }
461	        let segment = done.segments[index]
462	        let movie = segment.movieURL
463	        let name = movie.lastPathComponent
464	        let separate = done.choice.effectiveCursor == .separate
465	        guard let host = segment.screenHost else {
466	            return then(
467	                landed.withCursor(
468	                    url: nil,
469	                    problem: Self.cursorNoAnchorProblem(movieName: name, separate: separate),
470	                    image: nil))
471	        }
472	        let watchLost = segment.cursorWatchProblem ?? done.cursorWatchLost
473	        let size = CursorPixelSize(
474	            width: landed.descriptor.width, height: landed.descriptor.height)
475	        cursor.closeSegment(index, movieSize: size, anchor: CursorAnchor(kind: .e1, host: host)) {
476	            body in
477	            var url: URL?
478	            var writer: String?
479	            if let body {
480	                do {
481	                    url = try CursorFileWriter.write(body, forMovie: movie)
482	                } catch let problem as CursorFileProblem {
483	                    writer = problem.message
484	                } catch {
485	                    writer = "The cursor file for \(name) was not written: "
486	                        + error.localizedDescription
487	                }
488	            } else {
489	                writer = "The cursor file for \(name) was not written: no cursor was captured "
490	                    + "for it."
491	            }
492	            let problem = Self.cursorProblem(
493	                writer: writer, watchLost: watchLost, movieName: name, separate: separate)
494	            // The written file attached to the segment's media (spec §11 CU-34 (c)): the settle
495	            // probe ran before it existed. A failed attach leaves the segment as CU-18 left it.
496	            var attached: MediaCursor?
497	            if let url, case .success(let attachment) = MediaImporter.cursorAttachment(
498	                at: url, to: landed.descriptor)
499	            {
500	                attached = attachment.cursor
501	            }
502	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
503	                then(
504	                    landed.withCursor(
505	                        url: url, problem: problem,
506	                        image: url == nil ? nil : CursorImageMode.none, attached: attached))
507	            }
508	        }
509	    }
510	
511	    /// A window's frame in global points from the window list, or nil.
512	    private static func windowBounds(_ id: CGWindowID) -> CGRect? {
513	        guard
514	            let list = CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionIncludingWindow, id)
515	                as? [[String: Any]],
516	            let bounds = list.first?[kCGWindowBounds as String] as? NSDictionary
517	        else { return nil }
518	        return CGRect(dictionaryRepresentation: bounds as CFDictionary)
519	    }
520	
521	    /// A finite value above 0, else 1, so the header and the geometry always pass the core's
522	    /// check.
523	    private static func positive(_ value: Double) -> Double {
524	        value.isFinite && value > 0 ? value : 1
525	    }
526	}

529	/// A media whose cursor file could not be drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)): its id, the file's path
530	/// and the reason — the core's sentence, or `CursorTracks`' "the cursor file P could not be
531	/// read". The clip draws without a cursor and nothing fails; `export_status` answers it as a
532	/// `cursor_warnings` entry and `render_frame` as a sentence.
533	struct ExportCursorWarning: Equatable {
534	    let media: UInt32
535	    let path: String
536	    let message: String
537	}
538	
539	/// An export's and an offline frame's wait for the cursor tracks they draw (road map
540	/// creator-jobs CU3a2, spec §11 CU-37 (b)), in `withRampAudio`'s shape: published and wanted
541	/// on the caller's own `RecipeSource` key before the build, so no frame is composed while a
542	/// track it needs is still loading.
543	extension Exporter {
544	    /// Publishes `project`'s cursor files on `key`, then waits (`CursorTracks.wait` under
545	    /// owner `key`) for the requests: `at` nil every clip's, top level and every nest
546	    /// (`CursorFiles.requests`); `at` t only those the recipe at t (with `options`) names through
547	    /// its layers' `cursor` — the media's file at the layer's base `smoothing`. A
548	    /// `.failed(path, message)` records one warning per media on that path and waits again
549	    /// without it; `.cancelled` throws `ExportError.cancelled`. Never main: it blocks. The pin
550	    /// lasts until `key` is unregistered (`RecipeSource.unregister` releases it, CU-37 (e)).
551	    static func waitForCursors(
552	        project: ReelProject, key: Int, at: Ticks?, options: RecipeOptions,
553	        cancelled: @escaping () -> Bool
554	    ) throws -> [ExportCursorWarning] {
555	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
556	        let files = CursorFiles.files(of: snapshot)
557	        guard !files.isEmpty else { return [] }
558	        RecipeSource.shared.setCursorFiles(files, for: key)
559	        var requests: [CursorTrackRequest]
560	        if let t = at {
561	            var wanted = Set<CursorTrackRequest>()
562	            for layer in project.recipe(at: t, options: options)?.layers ?? [] {
563	                guard let cursor = layer.cursor, let file = files[cursor.media] else { continue }
564	                wanted.insert(CursorTrackRequest(url: file.url, smoothing: cursor.smoothing))
565	            }
566	            requests = wanted.sorted {
567	                $0.url.path != $1.url.path
568	                    ? $0.url.path < $1.url.path : $0.smoothing < $1.smoothing
569	            }
570	        } else {
571	            requests = CursorFiles.requests(of: snapshot, files: files)
572	        }
573	        var warnings: [ExportCursorWarning] = []
574	        while !requests.isEmpty {
575	            do {
576	                try CursorTracks.shared.wait(for: requests, owner: key, cancelled: cancelled)
577	                break
578	            } catch CursorTracks.WaitError.cancelled {
579	                throw ExportError.cancelled
580	            } catch CursorTracks.WaitError.failed(let path, let message) {
581	                for (media, file) in files.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key })
582	                where file.url.path == path {
583	                    warnings.append(ExportCursorWarning(media: media, path: path, message: message))
584	                }
585	                requests.removeAll { $0.url.path == path }
586	            }
587	        }
588	        return warnings
589	    }
590	
591	    /// `render_frame`'s sentence for each warning (CU-37 (c)), in order.
592	    static func cursorSentences(_ warnings: [ExportCursorWarning]) -> [String] {
593	        warnings.map { "The cursor of media \($0.media) is not drawn: \($0.message)." }
594	    }
595	
596	    /// A finished export's cursor count (spec §11 CU-38 (c)), after the graphic count:
597	    /// " 1 cursor warning" or " N cursor warnings", then " (hover for details)." or "."; "" for
598	    /// none.
599	    static func cursorWarningSuffix(
600	        _ warnings: [ExportCursorWarning], hover: Bool = true
601	    ) -> String {
602	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return "" }
603	        let count = warnings.count == 1 ? "1 cursor warning" : "\(warnings.count) cursor warnings"
604	        return " " + count + (hover ? " (hover for details)." : ".")
605	    }
606	
607	    /// The tooltip's list (CU-38 (c)): `cursorSentences`, one per line; nil for none.
608	    static func cursorWarningDetails(_ warnings: [ExportCursorWarning]) -> String? {
609	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
610	        return cursorSentences(warnings).joined(separator: "\n")
611	    }
612	}
613	//! The cursor file, format v1 (spec §11 CU-10): what a screen recording's
614	//! pointer, clicks, scrolls and keys were, written by the recorder beside
615	//! each segment movie as `<stem>.fjcursor` (CU-15) and read back through
616	//! `rc_cursor_open` before it is renamed into place. **This doc is the
617	//! format's specification**; `cursor_file_check.rs` holds the check and the
618	//! base64 decoder, `ffi_cursor.rs` the two exports.
619	//!
620	//! **The body** is one UTF-8 JSON object (CU-S4 `body=json`). Every time is
621	//! integer µs from the movie's first frame. Every position and length is
622	//! integer points × 100 in global display coordinates (`x`, `y`, a rect's
623	//! `[x, y, w, h]`, a size's `[w, h]`, an image's hot spot and size); a size
624	//! in px is an integer. The keys, every one required unless marked `?`:
625	//!
626	//! - `format` `"framejob-cursor"` · `version` 1 · `in_picture` bool ·
627	//!   `source` `"display"` | `"window"` | `"picked"` · `display_id?` u32.
628	//! - `source_frame` `[x, y, w, h]`, the SCDisplay or SCWindow frame at the
629	//!   segment's open (CU-S2's M3) · `point_size` `[w, h]` · `pixels_per_point`
630	//!   f64 · `content_size` `[w, h]` px, the stream's · `movie_size` `[w, h]`
631	//!   px, the written track's (CU-16), each side 1…16384.
632	//! - `anchor` `"e2"` | `"e1"`, the first frame the times count from, and
633	//!   `anchor_host_us` its host time (≥ 0) · `cursor_image`
634	//!   `"current-system"` | `"none"` (no images and no image changes).
635	//! - Columns, each an object of equal-length integer arrays sorted by time:
636	//!   `moves {t, x, y}`; `image_changes {t, id}`, `id` an index into
637	//!   `images`; `hidden {from, to}`, spans in order, each `to > from`, a span
638	//!   starting at or after the previous one's `to` (touching allowed);
639	//!   `clicks {t, button, down, x, y, count}`, `button` 0…31, `down` 0 or 1,
640	//!   `count` ≥ 1; `scrolls {t, x, y, dx, dy}`, `dx`/`dy` the event's point
641	//!   deltas as delivered (after the system's scroll direction; horizontal
642	//!   `dx`, vertical `dy`) × 100, signed, line deltas not stored;
643	//!   `dirty {t, x, y, w, h}`.
644	//! - `images`: `[{png, hot_x, hot_y, w, h, kind?}]`, its id its index: `png`
645	//!   is base64 (standard alphabet, padded) of a PNG, checked by its
646	//!   signature only (the core does no pixel work); the hot spot lies within
647	//!   `[0, w] × [0, h]`; `kind` one of `arrow`, `ibeam`, `ibeam_vertical`,
648	//!   `pointing_hand`, `open_hand`, `closed_hand`, `crosshair`,
649	//!   `operation_not_allowed`, `drag_copy`, `drag_link`, `contextual_menu`,
650	//!   `disappearing_item`, `resize_left`, `resize_right`, `resize_left_right`,
651	//!   `resize_up`, `resize_down`, `resize_up_down`.
652	//! - `geometry`: `[{t, screen_rect, content_rect, content_scale,
653	//!   scale_factor}]`, at least one entry, every CU-S2 candidate's inputs.
654	//! - `keys`: `{shortcut {t, keys, code}, typed {t}}`. A shortcut's `keys`
655	//!   is its spelled keys joined by `+` (`+` itself spelled `plus`), every
656	//!   token non-empty, without whitespace, holding `cmd` or `ctrl`, or holding
657	//!   `opt` with its last token one of `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS` (`left`,
658	//!   `right`, `up`, `down`, `delete`, `forwarddelete`, `return`, `enter`,
659	//!   `tab`, `esc`; spec §11 CU-60); `code` the layout-independent key code. A
660	//!   typed key is its time and nothing else (CU-7): no character, label or
661	//!   code of one can be stored.
662	//!
663	//! `hidden` and `dirty` stay empty until CU-S1 and CU-S3 pass. `keys` is
664	//! written from CU6 on, when a recording's Record shortcuts is on (CU-60);
665	//! every earlier file holds it empty. Floats (`pixels_per_point`, `content_scale`, `scale_factor`) must be
666	//! finite and above 0. The caps: [`MAX_MOVES`], [`MAX_SCROLLS`] and
667	//! [`MAX_DIRTY`] 1,728,000 each (4 h at 120 Hz); [`MAX_CLICKS`] 200,000;
668	//! [`MAX_IMAGES`] 1,024; one PNG [`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`] 1 MiB;
669	//! [`MAX_IMAGE_CHANGES`] 1,000,000; [`MAX_HIDDEN`], [`MAX_GEOMETRY`] and
670	//! [`MAX_SHORTCUTS`] 100,000; [`MAX_TYPED`] 1,000,000.
671	//!
672	//! **The parse order** ([`CursorFile::parse`]). A loose read first, as a
673	//! `serde_json::Value`: bytes that are not JSON ("the cursor file is not
674	//! JSON: …"), then not an object ("the cursor file is not a JSON object"),
675	//! then `format` absent or not `"framejob-cursor"` ("this is not a Frame Job
676	//! cursor file: its \"format\" is not \"framejob-cursor\""), then `version`
677	//! absent or not an integer ("the cursor file's \"version\" is not an
678	//! integer"), above [`RC_CURSOR_FILE_VERSION`] ("the cursor file is version
679	//! N; this Frame Job reads cursor files up to version 1") or below 1 ("the
680	//! cursor file is version N; versions start at 1"), then a `typed` object
681	//! holding any key but `t` ("keys.typed holds a typed key's time only;
682	//! \"<key>\" is refused (spec §11 CU-7)"). Only then the strict read, every
683	//! object `deny_unknown_fields`, through `serde_path_to_error` ("the cursor
684	//! file at \"<path>\": <serde's sentence>", "…at its top level: …" for the
685	//! root), so a newer file carrying keys v1 does not know is refused by its
686	//! version and a project's JSON by its format. Then each image's base64
687	//! ("images[i].png is not base64: …"), then `cursor_file_check::check`,
688	//! whose sentences are listed under **The check** below.
689	//!
690	//! **The check** (`cursor_file_check::check`), in order: the header's values (`anchor_host_us`, the floats, the two
691	//! sizes), then every column's lengths, the caps, the times, the hidden
692	//! spans, the images, the image changes, `cursor_image: "none"`, the clicks'
693	    static let cursorKey = "FrameJobRecordingCursor"
694	
695	    // MARK: - Metrics and vocabulary
696	
697	    /// Wider than `sheetWidth`: the microphone row is a popup AND a 120 pt
698	    /// meter beside the 106 pt label column, which 420 cannot hold.
699	    static let cardWidth: CGFloat = 500
700	    static let controlWidth: CGFloat = 200
701	    /// The Source popup's last row, "Window…", by tag; display rows carry
702	    /// their `CGDirectDisplayID` in `representedObject`.
703	    static let windowTag = 1
704	    static let countdownSeconds = 3
705	    static let rates = [30, 60]
706	    /// The note under Record shortcuts (spec §11 CU-60, CU-62).
707	    static let recordShortcutsSentence =
708	        "Records each shortcut you press with ⌘ or ⌃, or ⌥ with an arrow, Delete, Return, Tab "
709	        + "or Esc, and when you type, never what you type. Nothing is recorded while an app "
710	        + "holds secure input."
711	
712	    /// Where the panel is in a recording's life. `syncPhase()` draws it.
713	    enum Phase: Equatable {
714	        case idle
715	        case countdown(Int)
716	        case starting
717	        case recording
718	        case paused
719	        case stopping
720	        case landing
721	    }
722	
723	    var phase: Phase = .idle {
724	        didSet { syncPhase() }
725	    }
726	
727	    let recorder = ScreenRecorder.shared
728	
729	    // The controls — internal rather than private because the recording flow
730	    // lives in an extension in another file, and `private` does not cross one.
731	    let sourcePopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
732	    let includeFrameJobCheckbox = NSButton(
733	        checkboxWithTitle: "Include Frame Job windows", target: nil, action: nil)
734	    let cameraBesideCheckbox = NSButton(
735	        checkboxWithTitle: "Record the camera too", target: nil, action: nil)
736	    let cameraPopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
737	    let formatPopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
738	    let microphonePopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
739	    let enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox = NSButton(
740	        checkboxWithTitle: "Enhance the microphone when it lands", target: nil, action: nil)

742	    let systemAudioSwitch = NSSwitch()
743	    let showClicksSwitch = NSSwitch()

## Files and formats

Recordings are saved in **`~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`**, which Frame Job creates the first time it's needed. They're never stored inside the project package. To carry them into the package, use Consolidate (see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).

| File | Name | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Screen recording | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC (H.264 where HEVC isn't available), with system audio as one stereo 48 kHz track when System Audio is on |
| Its microphone | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC, beside the movie |
| Voice-over | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
| Camera recording | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie at the camera's format, HEVC (H.264 where HEVC isn't available), no sound of its own; its microphone file sits beside it as for a screen recording |
| Its cursor | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Beside every screen recording's movie (a display, a window or a picked window), one per stretch between pauses: where the pointer was about 120 times a second, every click and scroll, and how the recorded area sat on the screen. With Cursor set to In the picture, the pointer is drawn into the movie as well. If the file can't be written, the recording still lands and the panel's note says why |

When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.

The microphone is always a separate file from system audio, so you can set the level of your voice and the computer's sound independently. Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started and places the microphone clip to match, trimming its head if it started first.

### Frame rate

macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That rate comes from the file itself and isn't a fault. The **Rate** setting is the most frames per second the file can hold. A new project uses that setting as its frame rate, while the media entry keeps the file's real rate. Where the picture stops changing before the sound ends, the last frame is held to the end of the clip.

## The cursor

A recording's cursor file (`<name>.fjcursor`, beside its movie) travels with the movie into your project:

- **When a recording lands**, each stretch's movie gets its own cursor file.
- **When you import a movie**, by **File ▸ Add Media…**, a drop, opening it, or an agent's `import_media`, Frame Job looks beside it for a file with the same name ending in `.fjcursor`. It takes the file only when the file reads as a cursor file and was made for a movie of exactly this movie's size. A file that is missing, damaged or made for another size is left alone, and the movie imports without it. A copy Frame Job makes of a WebM or Matroska file is not looked beside.
- **When you relink a movie** (**Relink…**, the Media tab, or an agent's `relink_media`), Frame Job takes the cursor file beside the new movie. If there is none, it keeps the cursor file the media already had, as long as that file is still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file after the relink.
- **When you consolidate**, the cursor file is copied into the package beside its movie, and a moved package finds it there again (see [Consolidate Media](projects-and-media.md#consolidate-media)).

**On the Media tab.** Select a recording in the list and its **Cursor** section names its cursor file, or says "No cursor file", or adds "— missing" when the file has gone. **Locate…** chooses a `.fjcursor` file for it: Frame Job takes it only when it reads as a cursor file made for a movie of exactly this size, and otherwise says why and changes nothing (undo name "Locate Cursor File"). **Remove** forgets the cursor file, which stays on disk (undo name "Remove Cursor File").

*Agents:* `set_media_cursor` attaches, moves or removes a cursor file as **Locate…** and **Remove** do. `get_cursor_events` reads a recording's clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, typing stretches and pointer path, in the file's own time or in a clip's, with each click's place in the clip's zoom region frame.

**The Cursor section.** A clip whose movie has a cursor file the picture doesn't already show gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, after **Background**. It starts closed; its summary says **off**, **on** or **arrow**, with **+ ripples** when clicks ripple. Each row is its own undo step:

| Row | What it does | Range |
|---|---|---|
| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer from the file over the clip. On by default. | on, off |
| **Size** | How big the pointer is drawn. Quick picks 50, 100, 150, 200 and 400 %; the slider runs to 400 %, the field to 800 %. | 25–800 % |
| **Style** | **As recorded** draws the pointer images the file recorded. **Arrow** draws Frame Job's own arrow instead. | As recorded, Arrow |
| **Smoothing** | Calms a shaky path. The pointer still passes exactly through every click, at the moment of the click, and still holds still where it held still. | Off, Light, Medium, Strong |
| **Hide when idle** | Fades the pointer out after this long with no movement or click, and brings it back just before it next moves. | Never, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 s |
| **Clicks** | **Ripple** draws a ring growing out of every click. | None, Ripple |
| **Ripple color** | The ring's colour, with opacity. Live only while Clicks is Ripple. | any colour |
| **Ripple size** | How big the ring grows. Live only while Clicks is Ripple. | 25–400 % |

**Polish** sets Smoothing to Medium and Hide when idle to 3 s in one step.

With an action selected, **Size** and **Ripple size** animate across it. **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks** and **Ripple color** switch at the action's end. **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** belong to the clip, not to an action: their rows show ⊘ and they always change the clip itself. A clip with no cursor settings yet gets them the first time you change any row but Smoothing or Hide when idle with an action selected, so Size and Ripple size can animate rather than jump. Selecting clips that disagree shows a row mixed. **Reset** puts every row back to its default.

**The arrow.** Frame Job's own arrow is drawn crisp at any size, at the size of a standard pointer times **Size**. It is also what a clip draws when its cursor file recorded no pointer images, whichever **Style** is chosen.

**Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) carries a clip's cursor settings to another clip, with the rest of its picture settings.

**Motion blur.** With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0 (the Transform section, see [Motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur)), a moving pointer is drawn streaked along its path across the shutter, in the preview, `render_frame` and every export; a still pointer is drawn as it is. The click ripples stay sharp.

**What a recording lands with.** With **Cursor** set to **Separate**, macOS draws no pointer into the movie, the cursor file says the pointer is not in the picture, and the landed clip gets a **Cursor** section, with the pointer drawn as recorded. With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording (in a new project whose only other change is that, the undo name is "Cursor Clicks"). Nothing else is set: **Polish** is one click away. With **In the picture**, the pointer is in the movie, its cursor file says so, and the clip shows no **Cursor** section, so nothing is drawn twice.

### Shortcuts and Input Monitoring

With **Record shortcuts** ticked, a display or window recording also writes your keyboard into each stretch's cursor file, in two kinds:

- **A shortcut**, with its keys spelled out, for example `cmd+shift+4`. A key you press while holding ⌘ or ⌃ is a shortcut, and so is ⌥ with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc. ⇧ on its own never makes one, and neither does ⌥ with any other key (⌥E types é). The modifiers come first, in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`, then the key: a named key (`return`, `tab`, `space`, `left`, `f5` and so on) or the character the key types with no modifier, lowercased (`+` is spelled `plus`).
- **A typing mark**: the time of every other key you press, and of every key held down until it repeats. A typing mark never says which key it was. Frame Job doesn't read the character of a typed key at all.

**Nothing is recorded while any app holds secure input**, as a password field does: not a shortcut, not even a typing mark. A password field that doesn't turn secure input on, such as a Terminal `sudo` prompt with **Secure Keyboard Entry** off, is recorded as typing marks only, with no characters. Keys pressed while the recording is paused aren't recorded.

Recording keys needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission (see [Permissions](#permissions)). While it records, the menu-bar item shows the keyboard mark (see [The menu-bar item](#the-menu-bar-item)). *Agents:* `record_screen` with `keys: "shortcuts"`, and `get_cursor_events` reads the shortcuts and typing back.

## Permissions

A screen recording needs macOS's **Screen Recording** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**). A recording with a microphone, and every voice-over, also needs the **Microphone** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone**). A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission instead of Screen Recording, and a screen recording with **Record the camera too** needs both. Frame Job asks for each one when you press Record, before the countdown begins:

- **Screen Recording.** The first press without it shows macOS's prompt, and the panel explains what to do. Once you've turned it on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks you to, then press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane.
- **Microphone.** Asked only when a microphone is chosen. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears, and the countdown starts as soon as you allow it. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane.
- **Input Monitoring.** Asked only with **Record shortcuts** ticked and a display or window as the source (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring**), after Screen Recording and before the camera and the microphone. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it, so the first press both asks and opens System Settings at the Input Monitoring pane; the note says "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +." Turn Frame Job on there (add it with **+** if it isn't listed) and press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens the pane again. No relaunch is needed.
- **Camera.** Asked only with **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), after Screen Recording when there is a screen and before the microphone. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears; allowing it goes on to the microphone and the countdown, and denying it leaves the panel idle with a note. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane and the note says so.

While a system prompt or System Settings is up, the panel stops floating above other windows, so it doesn't cover them. It floats again on your next press of Record, or when the panel is opened again.

If Frame Job was started from a terminal or another app rather than from the Finder or the Dock, macOS applies that app's permissions instead of Frame Job's. In that case the panel's note names the launching process (by its pid) and says to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or to grant the permission to that app (the terminal, for a shell launch).

## Limits

- The panel records displays, single windows, a camera on its own, and a camera beside a display or a window. A camera records at one of its formats at that format's highest frame rate (not at a lower rate within the format's range). The panel lays a camera beside the screen out in one of five layouts, a corner always the bottom-right one; it has no control for another corner, Stacked, Screen Only, scale or inset. The layout's crop centres on the camera's picture, not on the person. There's no keystroke or callout overlay.
- When a stretch of a screen recording is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its other kept files, but it isn't added to the project. Only that stretch's microphone is.
- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the menu-bar item or the File menu.
- While a screen recording runs, the menu-bar item is the only place to pause or resume besides the File menu. If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch or in a crowded menu bar, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work.
- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the item was sized for.
- When a project is already at its track limit, a recording that needs a new track can't be added. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
- Record shortcuts writes nothing while any app holds secure input, and a typing mark is a time alone: there's no mode that records what you type.
- A **Separate** stretch whose cursor file couldn't be written (the screen never reported its start, or the file couldn't be saved) has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The landing's note says so, ending "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."

See also: [Audio](audio.md) for setting the microphone and system-audio levels, [Export](export.md) for writing the finished edit, and [Menus and shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md).

422	            }
423	        }
424	        let state: CursorState
425	        do {
426	            state = try track.state(
427	                at: Self.cursorTime(cursor, file: file),
428	                props: CursorStateProps(
429	                    smoothing: cursor.smoothing, hideIdle: cursor.hideIdle, scale: props.scale,
430	                    ripples: props.clicks == .ripple),
431	                ends: ends)
432	        } catch {

434	        }
435	        var sprite = placeholder
436	        var drawsSprite = false

438	        // image when the style is `recorded`, the frame has one and its texture is made; Frame

440	        if props.show, state.visible {
441	            if props.style == .recorded, let image = state.image,
442	               let texture = cursorSprites.texture(
443	                track: track, id: image.id, output: output, lift: { self.lifted($0) })
444	            {
445	                sprite = texture
446	                drawsSprite = true
447	                uniforms.cursorX = Float(state.x - image.hotX)
448	                uniforms.cursorY = Float(state.y - image.hotY)
449	                uniforms.cursorW = Float(image.w)
450	                uniforms.cursorH = Float(image.h)
451	            } else {
452	                let size = CursorArrow.pixelSize(pxPerPoint: state.pxPerPoint, scale: props.scale)
453	                if let texture = cursorSprites.arrow(
454	                    width: size.width, height: size.height, output: output,
455	                    lift: { self.lifted($0) })
456	                {
457	                    sprite = texture
458	                    drawsSprite = true
459	                    // 1:1 at (x − 1.5·W/14, y − 1.5·H/21, W, H): the tip on the hot spot.
460	                    let w = Double(size.width), h = Double(size.height)

462	                    uniforms.cursorX = Float(state.x - Double(hot.x) * w / Double(box.width))
463	                    uniforms.cursorY = Float(state.y - Double(hot.y) * h / Double(box.height))
464	                    uniforms.cursorW = Float(w)
465	                    uniforms.cursorH = Float(h)
466	                }
467	            }

469	                uniforms.cursorOpacity = Float(min(max(state.opacity, 0), 1))
470	                travel(cursor.shutter, ends: state.ends, at: state, uniforms: &uniforms)
471	            }
472	        }
473	        // Ripples (CU-33 (d)): the core answers them newest first; drawn oldest first.
474	        let ripples = props.clicks == .ripple ? Array(state.ripples.prefix(4).reversed()) : []
475	        if !ripples.isEmpty {
476	            let slots: [(WritableKeyPath<LayerUniforms, Float>,
477	                         WritableKeyPath<LayerUniforms, Float>,
478	                         WritableKeyPath<LayerUniforms, Float>)] = [
479	                (\.ripple0X, \.ripple0Y, \.ripple0Phase), (\.ripple1X, \.ripple1Y, \.ripple1Phase),
480	                (\.ripple2X, \.ripple2Y, \.ripple2Phase), (\.ripple3X, \.ripple3Y, \.ripple3Phase),
481	            ]
482	            for (ripple, slot) in zip(ripples, slots) {
483	                uniforms[keyPath: slot.0] = Float(ripple.x)
484	                uniforms[keyPath: slot.1] = Float(ripple.y)
485	                uniforms[keyPath: slot.2] = Float(min(max(ripple.phase, 0), 1))

488	            uniforms.rippleRadius = Float(24 * props.clickSize * state.pxPerPoint)

503	    /// The sprite's travel across the shutter (spec §11 CU-117 (e)): with o the drawn sprite's
504	    /// origin less the state's point, the origin moves to the first end + o and the travel is
505	    /// the second end less the first, drawn as `shutter.samples` sprite samples. No shutter, no
506	    /// answered ends, or ends that do not move leave the group at 0: the sprite draws once.
507	    private func travel(
508	        _ shutter: RecipeCursorShutter?, ends: [[Double]]?, at state: CursorState,
509	        uniforms: inout LayerUniforms
510	    ) {
511	        guard let shutter, let ends, ends.count == 2, ends[0].count >= 2, ends[1].count >= 2
512	        else { return }
513	        let dx = ends[1][0] - ends[0][0], dy = ends[1][1] - ends[0][1]
514	        guard dx != 0 || dy != 0 else { return }
515	        let ox = Double(uniforms.cursorX) - state.x, oy = Double(uniforms.cursorY) - state.y
516	        uniforms.cursorX = Float(ends[0][0] + ox)
517	        uniforms.cursorY = Float(ends[0][1] + oy)
518	        uniforms.cursorTravelX = Float(dx)
519	        uniforms.cursorTravelY = Float(dy)
520	        uniforms.cursorSamples = Float(shutter.samples)
521	    }

529	    /// `at`, a source tick in the stream the clip plays, as the cursor file's forward tick: itself
530	    /// forward; reversed, `pivot − at − frame`, at least 0 (CU-33 (f)). The shutter's ends are
531	    /// read through it too (CU-117 (e)).

533	        guard reversed else { return at }

541	        guard text.hasPrefix("#") else { return fallback }
542	        let hex = text.dropFirst()
543	        guard hex.count == 6 || hex.count == 8, let value = UInt32(hex, radix: 16) else {

547	        func channel(_ shift: UInt32) -> Float { Float((full >> shift) & 0xff) / 255 }

271	/// CU-7 as CU-60 amends it, PURE (road map creator-jobs CU6): which key-down is a shortcut and
272	/// how it is spelled; `CursorCapture+Keys.swift` is the live source that feeds it.
273	///
274	/// **The rule**, in order: secure input held by any process (read at delivery) → nothing, not
275	/// even a time; an auto-repeat → a typed mark; ⌘ or ⌃ held, or ⌥ held with an arrow, Delete,
276	/// Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc (`optionKeyCodes`, the owner's answer of
277	/// 2026-11-01) → a shortcut; anything else → a typed mark. ⇧ alone never makes a shortcut, and
278	/// ⌥ with any other key types a character (⌥E is é), so it is typed.
279	///
280	/// **The spelling**: the held modifiers in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`, then the
281	/// key — `namedKeys` by its virtual key code, else the character lowercased, `+` spelled `plus`,
282	/// and an empty, whitespace or control character `key<code>` — joined by `+`, so the core's
283	/// check (`cursor_file_check.rs`) accepts every one this writes.
284	enum CursorKeyFilter {
285	    /// ← → ↓ ↑ (123 124 125 126), Delete (51), Forward Delete (117), Return (36), keypad Enter
286	    /// (76), Tab (48) and Esc (53): the keys ⌥ alone makes a shortcut of. Their spellings are
287	    /// the core's `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`.
288	    static let optionKeyCodes: Set<Int> = [123, 124, 125, 126, 51, 117, 36, 76, 48, 53]
289	
290	    /// The keys spelled by name, by their kVK codes (Carbon's `Events.h`).
291	    static let namedKeys: [Int: String] = [
292	        36: "return", 76: "enter", 48: "tab", 49: "space", 51: "delete", 117: "forwarddelete",
293	        53: "esc", 123: "left", 124: "right", 125: "down", 126: "up", 115: "home", 119: "end",
294	        116: "pageup", 121: "pagedown", 114: "help",
295	        122: "f1", 120: "f2", 99: "f3", 118: "f4", 96: "f5", 97: "f6", 98: "f7", 100: "f8",
296	        101: "f9", 109: "f10", 103: "f11", 111: "f12", 105: "f13", 107: "f14", 113: "f15",
297	        106: "f16", 64: "f17", 79: "f18", 80: "f19", 90: "f20",
298	    ]
299	
300	    /// Whether the key-down is a shortcut: not an auto-repeat, and ⌘ or ⌃ held, or ⌥ held with
301	    /// one of `optionKeyCodes`. The source reads a character only when this is true.
302	    static func isShortcut(_ event: CursorKeyEvent) -> Bool {
303	        guard !event.isRepeat else { return false }
304	        if event.modifiers.contains(.cmd) || event.modifiers.contains(.ctrl) { return true }
305	        return event.modifiers.contains(.opt) && optionKeyCodes.contains(event.keyCode)
306	    }
307	
308	    /// The shortcut's `+`-joined spelling (the type doc).
309	    static func spelled(_ event: CursorKeyEvent) -> String {
310	        var tokens: [String] = []
311	        if event.modifiers.contains(.cmd) { tokens.append("cmd") }
312	        if event.modifiers.contains(.ctrl) { tokens.append("ctrl") }
313	        if event.modifiers.contains(.opt) { tokens.append("opt") }
314	        if event.modifiers.contains(.shift) { tokens.append("shift") }
315	        tokens.append(keyName(event))
316	        return tokens.joined(separator: "+")
317	    }
318	
319	    /// The key's own token: its name, else its character, else `key<code>`.
320	    private static func keyName(_ event: CursorKeyEvent) -> String {
321	        if let name = namedKeys[event.keyCode] { return name }
322	        let character = (event.character ?? "").lowercased()
323	        let plain =
324	            !character.isEmpty
325	            && character.unicodeScalars.allSatisfy { scalar in
326	                !scalar.properties.isWhitespace
327	                    && scalar.properties.generalCategory != .control
328	                    && scalar.properties.generalCategory != .format
329	            }
330	        guard plain else { return "key\(event.keyCode)" }
331	        return character.replacingOccurrences(of: "+", with: "plus")
332	    }
333	
334	    /// The whole rule (the type doc): `secure` is `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` at delivery.
335	    static func entry(for event: CursorKeyEvent, secure: Bool) -> CursorKeyEntry {
336	        if secure { return .none }
337	        if event.isRepeat { return .typed }
338	        guard isShortcut(event) else { return .typed }
339	        return .shortcut(keys: spelled(event), code: event.keyCode)
340	    }
341	}

345	/// Every screen recording's cursor file (road map creator-jobs CU1b1, spec §11 CU-11…CU-13,
346	/// CU-18): the segments' header and opening geometry, the capture's start with segment 0 open,

350	/// **The anchor is E1** (CU-12): a segment's times count from its screen did-start's host time,
351	/// stamped on every segment by `+Delegates.swift`; E2 is never used for a cursor file. A landed
352	/// segment with no E1 gets no file. **The geometry** comes from the frame watch (CU-13); a watch
353	/// that could not go on the stream (at the start, with no camera, or at the segment's resume)

364	    /// The header and opening geometry every segment's file starts from (CU-13), before any
365	    /// frame: `scale_factor` the filter's `pointPixelScale`; `content_scale` the stream's
366	    /// configured pixel width ÷ (scale factor × point width); `content_rect` (0, 0, the point
367	    /// size × content scale); `screen_rect` the source's frame — `CGDisplayBounds` for a
368	    /// display, the window list's `kCGWindowBounds` for a window (the filter's `contentRect`
369	    /// when the list has none, whose origin may be window-local rather than global points
370	    /// until the first frame's geometry replaces it), the filter's `contentRect` for a picked
371	    /// source. The header's
372	    /// `pixels_per_point` is the configured width ÷ the point width; `in_picture` the choice's
373	    /// (spec §11 CU-31: true only In the picture, where the stream burns the pointer in);
374	    /// `cursor_image` none (CU-S1).
375	    static func cursorStart(
376	        filter: SCContentFilter, choice: RecordingChoice, stream: SCStreamConfiguration
377	    ) -> CursorSegmentStart {
378	        let points = filter.contentRect.size
379	        let width = Double(max(stream.width, 1))
380	        let height = Double(max(stream.height, 1))
381	        let scaleFactor = positive(Double(filter.pointPixelScale))
382	        let pixelsPerPoint = positive(points.width > 0 ? width / Double(points.width) : 1)
383	        let contentScale = positive(
384	            points.width > 0 ? width / (scaleFactor * Double(points.width)) : 1)
385	        let source: CursorSourceKind
386	        let displayID: UInt32?
387	        let frame: CGRect
388	        switch choice.source {
389	        case .display(let id):
390	            source = .display
391	            displayID = id
392	            frame = CGDisplayBounds(id)
393	        case .window(let id):
394	            source = .window
395	            displayID = nil
396	            frame = windowBounds(id) ?? filter.contentRect
397	        case .picked, .voiceOver, .camera:
398	            source = .picked
399	            displayID = nil
400	            frame = filter.contentRect
401	        }
402	        let geometry = CursorGeometry(
403	            screenRect: frame,
404	            contentRect: CGRect(
405	                x: 0, y: 0, width: Double(points.width) * contentScale,
406	                height: Double(points.height) * contentScale),
407	            contentScale: contentScale, scaleFactor: scaleFactor)
408	        return CursorSegmentStart(
409	            inPicture: choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture, source: source,
410	            displayID: displayID, sourceFrame: frame,
411	            pointSize: points, pixelsPerPoint: pixelsPerPoint,
412	            contentSize: CursorPixelSize(
413	                width: min(Int(width), 16384), height: min(Int(height), 16384)),

## Files and formats

Recordings are saved in **`~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`**, which Frame Job creates the first time it's needed. They're never stored inside the project package. To carry them into the package, use Consolidate (see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).

| File | Name | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Screen recording | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC (H.264 where HEVC isn't available), with system audio as one stereo 48 kHz track when System Audio is on |
| Its microphone | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC, beside the movie |
| Voice-over | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
| Camera recording | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie at the camera's format, HEVC (H.264 where HEVC isn't available), no sound of its own; its microphone file sits beside it as for a screen recording |
| Its cursor | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Beside every screen recording's movie (a display, a window or a picked window), one per stretch between pauses: where the pointer was about 120 times a second, every click and scroll, and how the recorded area sat on the screen. With Cursor set to In the picture, the pointer is drawn into the movie as well. If the file can't be written, the recording still lands and the panel's note says why |

When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.

The microphone is always a separate file from system audio, so you can set the level of your voice and the computer's sound independently. Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started and places the microphone clip to match, trimming its head if it started first.

### Frame rate

macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That rate comes from the file itself and isn't a fault. The **Rate** setting is the most frames per second the file can hold. A new project uses that setting as its frame rate, while the media entry keeps the file's real rate. Where the picture stops changing before the sound ends, the last frame is held to the end of the clip.

## The cursor

A recording's cursor file (`<name>.fjcursor`, beside its movie) travels with the movie into your project:

- **When a recording lands**, each stretch's movie gets its own cursor file.
- **When you import a movie**, by **File ▸ Add Media…**, a drop, opening it, or an agent's `import_media`, Frame Job looks beside it for a file with the same name ending in `.fjcursor`. It takes the file only when the file reads as a cursor file and was made for a movie of exactly this movie's size. A file that is missing, damaged or made for another size is left alone, and the movie imports without it. A copy Frame Job makes of a WebM or Matroska file is not looked beside.
- **When you relink a movie** (**Relink…**, the Media tab, or an agent's `relink_media`), Frame Job takes the cursor file beside the new movie. If there is none, it keeps the cursor file the media already had, as long as that file is still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file after the relink.
- **When you consolidate**, the cursor file is copied into the package beside its movie, and a moved package finds it there again (see [Consolidate Media](projects-and-media.md#consolidate-media)).

**On the Media tab.** Select a recording in the list and its **Cursor** section names its cursor file, or says "No cursor file", or adds "— missing" when the file has gone. **Locate…** chooses a `.fjcursor` file for it: Frame Job takes it only when it reads as a cursor file made for a movie of exactly this size, and otherwise says why and changes nothing (undo name "Locate Cursor File"). **Remove** forgets the cursor file, which stays on disk (undo name "Remove Cursor File").

*Agents:* `set_media_cursor` attaches, moves or removes a cursor file as **Locate…** and **Remove** do. `get_cursor_events` reads a recording's clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, typing stretches and pointer path, in the file's own time or in a clip's, with each click's place in the clip's zoom region frame.

**The Cursor section.** A clip whose movie has a cursor file the picture doesn't already show gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, after **Background**. It starts closed; its summary says **off**, **on** or **arrow**, with **+ ripples** when clicks ripple. Each row is its own undo step:

| Row | What it does | Range |
|---|---|---|
| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer from the file over the clip. On by default. | on, off |
| **Size** | How big the pointer is drawn. Quick picks 50, 100, 150, 200 and 400 %; the slider runs to 400 %, the field to 800 %. | 25–800 % |
| **Style** | **As recorded** draws the pointer images the file recorded. **Arrow** draws Frame Job's own arrow instead. | As recorded, Arrow |
| **Smoothing** | Calms a shaky path. The pointer still passes exactly through every click, at the moment of the click, and still holds still where it held still. | Off, Light, Medium, Strong |
| **Hide when idle** | Fades the pointer out after this long with no movement or click, and brings it back just before it next moves. | Never, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 s |
| **Clicks** | **Ripple** draws a ring growing out of every click. | None, Ripple |
| **Ripple color** | The ring's colour, with opacity. Live only while Clicks is Ripple. | any colour |
| **Ripple size** | How big the ring grows. Live only while Clicks is Ripple. | 25–400 % |

**Polish** sets Smoothing to Medium and Hide when idle to 3 s in one step.

With an action selected, **Size** and **Ripple size** animate across it. **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks** and **Ripple color** switch at the action's end. **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** belong to the clip, not to an action: their rows show ⊘ and they always change the clip itself. A clip with no cursor settings yet gets them the first time you change any row but Smoothing or Hide when idle with an action selected, so Size and Ripple size can animate rather than jump. Selecting clips that disagree shows a row mixed. **Reset** puts every row back to its default.

**The arrow.** Frame Job's own arrow is drawn crisp at any size, at the size of a standard pointer times **Size**. It is also what a clip draws when its cursor file recorded no pointer images, whichever **Style** is chosen.

**Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) carries a clip's cursor settings to another clip, with the rest of its picture settings.

**Motion blur.** With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0 (the Transform section, see [Motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur)), a moving pointer is drawn streaked along its path across the shutter, in the preview, `render_frame` and every export; a still pointer is drawn as it is. The click ripples stay sharp.

**What a recording lands with.** With **Cursor** set to **Separate**, macOS draws no pointer into the movie, the cursor file says the pointer is not in the picture, and the landed clip gets a **Cursor** section, with the pointer drawn as recorded. With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording (in a new project whose only other change is that, the undo name is "Cursor Clicks"). Nothing else is set: **Polish** is one click away. With **In the picture**, the pointer is in the movie, its cursor file says so, and the clip shows no **Cursor** section, so nothing is drawn twice.

### Shortcuts and Input Monitoring

With **Record shortcuts** ticked, a display or window recording also writes your keyboard into each stretch's cursor file, in two kinds:

- **A shortcut**, with its keys spelled out, for example `cmd+shift+4`. A key you press while holding ⌘ or ⌃ is a shortcut, and so is ⌥ with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc. ⇧ on its own never makes one, and neither does ⌥ with any other key (⌥E types é). The modifiers come first, in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`, then the key: a named key (`return`, `tab`, `space`, `left`, `f5` and so on) or the character the key types with no modifier, lowercased (`+` is spelled `plus`).
- **A typing mark**: the time of every other key you press, and of every key held down until it repeats. A typing mark never says which key it was. Frame Job doesn't read the character of a typed key at all.

**Nothing is recorded while any app holds secure input**, as a password field does: not a shortcut, not even a typing mark. A password field that doesn't turn secure input on, such as a Terminal `sudo` prompt with **Secure Keyboard Entry** off, is recorded as typing marks only, with no characters. Keys pressed while the recording is paused aren't recorded.

Recording keys needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission (see [Permissions](#permissions)). While it records, the menu-bar item shows the keyboard mark (see [The menu-bar item](#the-menu-bar-item)). *Agents:* `record_screen` with `keys: "shortcuts"`, and `get_cursor_events` reads the shortcuts and typing back.

## Permissions

A screen recording needs macOS's **Screen Recording** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**). A recording with a microphone, and every voice-over, also needs the **Microphone** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone**). A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission instead of Screen Recording, and a screen recording with **Record the camera too** needs both. Frame Job asks for each one when you press Record, before the countdown begins:

- **Screen Recording.** The first press without it shows macOS's prompt, and the panel explains what to do. Once you've turned it on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks you to, then press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane.
- **Microphone.** Asked only when a microphone is chosen. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears, and the countdown starts as soon as you allow it. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane.
- **Input Monitoring.** Asked only with **Record shortcuts** ticked and a display or window as the source (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring**), after Screen Recording and before the camera and the microphone. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it, so the first press both asks and opens System Settings at the Input Monitoring pane; the note says "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +." Turn Frame Job on there (add it with **+** if it isn't listed) and press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens the pane again. No relaunch is needed.
- **Camera.** Asked only with **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), after Screen Recording when there is a screen and before the microphone. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears; allowing it goes on to the microphone and the countdown, and denying it leaves the panel idle with a note. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane and the note says so.

While a system prompt or System Settings is up, the panel stops floating above other windows, so it doesn't cover them. It floats again on your next press of Record, or when the panel is opened again.

If Frame Job was started from a terminal or another app rather than from the Finder or the Dock, macOS applies that app's permissions instead of Frame Job's. In that case the panel's note names the launching process (by its pid) and says to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or to grant the permission to that app (the terminal, for a shell launch).

## Limits

- The panel records displays, single windows, a camera on its own, and a camera beside a display or a window. A camera records at one of its formats at that format's highest frame rate (not at a lower rate within the format's range). The panel lays a camera beside the screen out in one of five layouts, a corner always the bottom-right one; it has no control for another corner, Stacked, Screen Only, scale or inset. The layout's crop centres on the camera's picture, not on the person. There's no keystroke or callout overlay.
- When a stretch of a screen recording is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its other kept files, but it isn't added to the project. Only that stretch's microphone is.
- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the menu-bar item or the File menu.
- While a screen recording runs, the menu-bar item is the only place to pause or resume besides the File menu. If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch or in a crowded menu bar, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work.
- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the item was sized for.
- When a project is already at its track limit, a recording that needs a new track can't be added. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
- Record shortcuts writes nothing while any app holds secure input, and a typing mark is a time alone: there's no mode that records what you type.
- A **Separate** stretch whose cursor file couldn't be written (the screen never reported its start, or the file couldn't be saved) has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The landing's note says so, ending "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."

See also: [Audio](audio.md) for setting the microphone and system-audio levels, [Export](export.md) for writing the finished edit, and [Menus and shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md).

---
title: "Style the recorded cursor"
description: Change how a recording's pointer looks after you've recorded it, from its size and path to when it hides and a ring on every click.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When a screen recording keeps its pointer out of the movie, Frame Job draws the pointer for you, so you can restyle it long after you stopped recording. The **Cursor** section makes it bigger, calms a shaky path, hides it when it rests and puts a ring on every click.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor"
  tools={['set_video', 'paste_attributes']}
  needs="A recording whose cursor file isn't already in the picture. That's every recording made with Cursor set to Separate, the default."
/>

## Find the Cursor section

Select a recording's clip, open the **Clip** tab's **Picture** sub-tab and look after **Background**. The section starts shut. Its header sums up what's set: **off**, **on** or **arrow**, with **+ ripples** when clicks ripple.

The section is there only when every selected clip comes from a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) that the picture doesn't already show:

- A recording made with **Cursor:** set to **In the picture** has no section, because the pointer is part of the movie and would otherwise be drawn twice. See [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).
- A movie with no cursor file has no section. If the file exists but didn't come along, [attach it with Locate…](/recording/cursor-files/#attach-or-re-point-a-cursor-file).
- A selection that also holds any other kind of clip has no section.

A freeze frame of a recording has the section too, with the pointer held where it was on that frame.

Each row is its own undo step. If the selected clips disagree about a row, it shows as mixed.

## Tidy the pointer in one click

Choose **Polish** at the bottom of the section. It sets **Smoothing** to **Medium** and **Hide when idle** to **3 s**, as one undo step called "Polish Cursor". Nothing else changes, and you can adjust either row afterwards.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer. | On | On, off |
| **Size** | How big the pointer is drawn. | 100 % | 25–800 % |
| **Style** | Which pointer is drawn. | As recorded | As recorded, Arrow |
| **Smoothing** | Calms a shaky path. | Off | Off, Light, Medium, Strong |
| **Hide when idle** | Fades out a resting pointer. | Never | Never, 1, 2, 3, 5 or 10 s |
| **Clicks** | Draws a ring out of every click. | None | None, Ripple |
| **Ripple color** | The ring's colour, with opacity. | White at 80 % | Any colour |
| **Ripple size** | How big the ring grows. | 100 % | 25–400 % |

## Show or resize the pointer

Untick **Show cursor** to draw no pointer on this clip. Click rings are separate, so with **Clicks** set to **Ripple** the rings still draw without a pointer. That's useful when you want to show where someone clicked and nothing else.

**Size** has quick picks at 50, 100, 150, 200 and 400 %. Its slider runs to 400 %, and you can type up to 800 % in the field.

## Choose the pointer's style

**Style** offers **As recorded** and **Arrow**. Frame Job's recordings don't store pictures of the pointer, so both choices draw Frame Job's arrow, and a pointer that was an I-beam or a hand on screen is drawn as the arrow too. The only difference you'll see is that the section's header reads **arrow** rather than **on**.

Frame Job's arrow is a black arrow with a white outline, 14 by 21 points at 100 %. It's drawn at the recording's own pixel density and redrawn for each **Size** rather than stretched, so it stays crisp.

## Calm a shaky path

**Smoothing** irons out the wobble in the pointer's path, from **Light** through **Medium** to **Strong**. The pointer still reaches every click exactly, at the moment of the click, and a pause stays a pause.

## Hide a resting pointer

**Hide when idle** fades the pointer out after the time you pick with no movement and no mouse press. Scrolling and typing don't count as activity. The fade takes 0.2 s, and the pointer comes back 0.15 s before it next moves or clicks, so it's already there when it sets off.

## Show clicks

Set **Clicks** to **Ripple** to draw a ring growing out of every press of a mouse button. A ring lasts 0.45 s, growing quickly at first and fading as it goes, and up to four can show at once. At 100 % it reaches 24 points from the click.

**Ripple color** and **Ripple size** are live only while **Clicks** is **Ripple**. **Ripple size** has quick picks at 50, 100, 150 and 200 %.

**Clicks** starts at **None**, unless the recording was made with **Show Clicks:** on and **Cursor:** set to **Separate**. Those clips land with **Ripple** already set.

## Put everything back

**Reset** in the section's header appears once something differs from its default. It sets all eight rows back to the defaults in the table, as one undo step called "Reset Cursor".

## Change the pointer part-way through a clip

Select an [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip and the section edits that action instead of the whole clip:

| Rows | With an action selected |
| --- | --- |
| **Size**, **Ripple size** | Animate across the action. |
| **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** | Switch at the action's end. |
| **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** | Always change the clip itself. Their rows show ⊘. |

**Polish** also changes the clip itself, whatever is selected. **Reset** with an action selected puts the first six rows back at that action's end, and **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle** back on the clip.

The first time you change one of the action rows on a clip with no cursor settings of its own, Frame Job stores the defaults on the clip in the same step. That's what lets **Size** and **Ripple size** animate from 100 % instead of jumping.

## Copy the settings to another clip

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) carries a clip's cursor settings to another clip, along with the rest of its picture settings. The settings are replaced as a whole, so pasting from a clip whose cursor you never changed puts the target's back to the defaults. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

## Streak a moving pointer

With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0, in the **Transform** section, a moving pointer is streaked along its path across the shutter. That happens even when the clip itself stands still, so a fast flick across the screen looks natural in an otherwise static recording. A still pointer and the click rings stay sharp.

The streak shows in the preview, in rendered frames and in every export. A clip that [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp keeps its pointer sharp, and so does a freeze frame.

## How the pointer sits in the picture

The pointer is drawn inside its clip, as if it were part of the movie. So it follows the clip's zooms, placement and crop, it takes the clip's grade, and the preview, rendered frames and exports all agree. In an HLG project the pointer and its rings are lifted to match the picture.

It also follows the clip's time. Change the clip's speed and the pointer speeds up with it. [Reverse the clip](/speed/reverse/) and the pointer plays backwards too.

## Good to know

- A cursor file loads in the background and never holds up the preview. Until it's ready the frame draws without the pointer, then redraws with it. Changing **Smoothing** can do the same for a moment, because the new path has to be worked out. Rendered frames and exports wait for the file.
- **Hide when idle** and the ring's 0.45 s count in the recording's own time, so on a clip at 2× they pass twice as fast.
- [Splitting](/editing/split/) a clip or making a freeze frame keeps the clip's own **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle**, even from inside an action.
- Paste onto a clip with no cursor file and the settings are kept but nothing is drawn.
- If a cursor file is missing or can't be read, the clip draws with no pointer. See [When a cursor file has a problem](/recording/cursor-files/#when-a-cursor-file-has-a-problem).

## With an agent

`set_video` sets the same eight values, and it isn't held to the pop-ups' steps: **Smoothing** can be any value from 0 to 1, and **Hide when idle** anything from 0.5 to 30 seconds. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/)
- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/)
